title: Conformance findings
description: What the conformance lens may say. It is the only step that reads the stated intent, so it is the only one that can invent a requirement - and inventing one is worse than missing a mismatch, because a fabricated requirement sounds authoritative and sends a reader to argue with a document that never said it. Hence two anchors: the code side quoted from the file, and the requirement side quoted from the intent.

findings.description: Empty is a valid and frequent answer. Most changes match their stated intent, and a change that simply does more than the intent describes is usually not a defect.

line.description: 1-indexed line in the numbered file where the divergence shows.

snippet.description: The code, copied verbatim from the numbered listing. Checked by exact search near `line`.

requirement.description: The sentence or clause from the stated intent, **copied verbatim**. It is checked by exact search against the intent you were given. Do not paraphrase it, do not summarise several sentences into one, and do not state a requirement you believe is implied - if you cannot quote it, it is not a requirement.

mismatch.description: What the code does instead, in one or two sentences.

glossary.unimplemented: the intent requires something and the change does not do it
glossary.contradicts: the change does the opposite of what the intent says
glossary.undocumented: the change does something substantial the intent does not mention - report only when it changes behaviour somebody depends on, not for every helper
glossary.stale-intent: the code is right and the document is out of date - say so, this is often the most useful thing you can report

glossary.blocking: merging this ships behaviour the intent forbids, or omits something it requires outright
glossary.significant: a real divergence on a path somebody uses, but bounded
glossary.minor: a real divergence with little consequence, or a wording gap
